newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian rebels in Vlore sign deal with Italy-ANSA.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rebels in Vlore sign deal with Italy-ANSA.

text.p: Rebel leaders from the southern Albanian port of Vlore signed a declaration with Italy on Monday undertaking to restore order in the town and encourage civilians to lay down their weapons, the Italian news agency ANSA said.

It reported from on board the Italian amphibious assault ship San Giorgio in the Adriatic, where Italy's ambassador to Tirana, Paolo Foresti, was meeting rebel leaders. The Italian Foreign Ministry could not immediately confirm the ANSA report.

Italian RAI television carried a similar report from on board the San Giorgio. It said Foresti had met eight representatives from a citizens' committee from the port, which is at the epicentre of an armed uprising in southern Albania.
ANSA said the declaration asked Italy and the international community for emergency aid and undertook "to favour the immediate handing back of weapons in the hands of the citizens of Valona".

The rebel representatives also asked in the declaration for "guarantees" that an agreement signed by Albanian President Sali Berisha and political parties in Tirana on Sunday to resolve the crisis peacefully would be applied correctly and rapidly.

The accord provides for an all-party government and new elections by June under international supervision. It gives rebels a week to hand in their weapons and asks parliament to declare an amnesty for all those implicated in the revolt.
